acceptance.given: Runtime evidence capture is configured with declared append-only evidence boundaries and existing historical artifacts.

oracle.expected: Evidence records are appended only within declared boundaries while historical bytes remain unchanged.
forbidden: Overwriting or mutating frozen historical evidence
oracle.observable: A filesystem/content check compares pre/post historical bytes and verifies each new record path is an allowed append target.

acceptance.then: The boundary checker reports append-only additions at allowed paths and unchanged historical artifacts.
acceptance.when: During runtime-evidence capture, evaluate write locations and compare frozen historical artifacts before and after the run.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Inject a runtime-evidence write outside the declared boundary or alter a frozen historical artifact; the boundary and byte-integrity check must fail.

affected_subjects: Runtime evidence append boundary and historical artifact preservation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce append-only runtime evidence within declared boundaries and reject historical artifact mutation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; preserve existing evidence records and append semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Undeclared or mutating writes are rejected; valid captures append new evidence records only.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Boundary and historical-byte checks pass for valid capture and fail for any out-of-bound or overwrite attempt.

acceptance.given: Replay, seed, matrix, review, and Quick Dev artifacts expose authorization-set data.

oracle.expected: Each specified artifact exposes a machine-verifiable authorization set containing zero entries.
oracle.observable: A schema-aware inspection parses each artifact's authorization set and counts exactly zero entries.

acceptance.then: The machine check returns an empty authorization set for every named artifact.
acceptance.when: Run the artifact authorization inspection against replay, seed, matrix, review, and Quick Dev outputs.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Provide a named artifact containing one authorization entry or an unparsable authorization field; the emptiness validator must fail.

affected_subjects: Replay, seed, matrix, review, and Quick Dev artifact authorization sets
slice_hint.behavior_change: Expose and validate zero-entry authorization sets for all specified artifact classes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Authorization representation remains backward-compatible; only emptiness validation is enforced.

slice_hint.state_transition: Artifacts with non-empty or unverifiable authorization sets are rejected; valid artifacts expose zero entries.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five artifact categories parse successfully and each authorization set length equals zero.

acceptance.given: A verdict is produced together with current source identity records and real execution artifacts.

oracle.expected: The verdict evidence basis consists of verified source identity and real execution outputs, with assistant prose excluded.
forbidden: Assistant prose is used as evidentiary basis
Verdict accepted solely from assistant prose
oracle.observable: Evidence manifest inspection shows source hashes/identities and execution records linked to the verdict, and no prose field is accepted as proof.

acceptance.then: The verifier accepts the verdict only when source identity and execution evidence are present and prose-only support is rejected.
acceptance.when: At verdict evaluation time, inspect and validate the evidence manifest and provenance links.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Submit a verdict whose only support is assistant prose or whose source/execution provenance is missing; provenance validation must fail.

affected_subjects: Verdict evidence provenance and source/execution basis
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require current source identity and real execution artifacts as the sole machine-validated verdict basis.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema break; retain existing provenance fields and reject prose-only evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Prose-only verdicts become invalid; provenance-backed verdicts remain evaluable.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation succeeds only with matching source identity and execution evidence links and fails when prose is the sole basis.

acceptance.given: Pinned inputs and their baseline semantic verdict are available for a clean checkout replay.

oracle.expected: Executing the pinned inputs in a fresh checkout reproduces the baseline semantic verdict exactly.
forbidden: Verdict cannot be reproduced from pinned inputs
oracle.observable: The replay comparison reports identical normalized semantic verdicts for baseline and fresh-checkout executions.

acceptance.then: The reproducibility check passes only when fresh-checkout and pinned-input verdicts are equal.
acceptance.when: Provision a fresh checkout, execute with pinned inputs, and compare its normalized semantic verdict to the recorded baseline.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Replay pinned inputs in a fresh checkout with a deliberately changed semantic result; the reproducibility comparison must observe a mismatch and fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Deterministically compare fresh-checkout replay verdicts against the pinned-input baseline and reject drift.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No state migration; preserve baseline format and normalized verdict comparison.

slice_hint.state_transition: Fresh replay yields pass on exact match and fail on any semantic verdict drift.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A clean checkout run with pinned inputs produces a normalized verdict byte-equivalent to baseline; any difference causes failure.
